verses.text: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, He made him in His own likeness.
Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. And in the day they were created, He called them "man."
When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image; and he named him Seth.
And after he had become the father of Seth, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.
When Seth was 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.
And after he had become the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died.
When Enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.
And after he had become the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and then he died.
When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.
And after he had become the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died.
When Mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.
And after he had become the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died.
When Jared was 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.
And after he had become the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Jared lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.
When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.
And after he had become the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.
Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.
When Methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.
And after he had become the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.
When Lamech was 182 years old, he had a son.
And he named him Noah, saying, "May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed."
And after he had become the father of Noah, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.
After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Narrative of beginnings (Genesis 1-11): creation, the first family, the flood and the nations, with genealogies
context.audience: Israel, God’s covenant people, learning who their God is, where the world came from and what went wrong with it
context.setting: “This is the book of the generations of Adam” (v.1). God made mankind in His likeness, and Adam had a son “in his own likeness, after his own image,” Seth (vv.1-3). Ten generations follow, each with the same pattern: he lived so many years and had a son, then he lived on and had other sons and daughters, and “then he died.” The ages are very great: Adam 930 years (v.5), Methuselah 969, the longest of all (v.27). One man breaks the pattern: “Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away” (v.24). The list ends with Lamech, who names his son Noah, saying, “May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands” (v.29), and Noah has three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth (v.32).
context.custom: Ancient peoples kept genealogies to tie families to land and to the past. The Sumerian King List from Mesopotamia names kings before the flood who reigned for tens of thousands of years; the ages in Genesis 5 are far smaller, though still beyond any life we know. The numbers differ in the Hebrew, the Greek Septuagint and the Samaritan copies, and readers have long debated whether they are meant literally, or to show how life ran down after the fall.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 6 tells of the wickedness that filled the earth, God’s grief, and His command to Noah to build an ark.
context.timelineBible: Luke’s genealogy of Jesus runs back through these names to “Adam, the son of God” (Luke 3:36-38). Hebrews says Enoch was taken “so that he did not see death” (Hebrews 11:5) because he pleased God (Hebrews 11:5), and Jude quotes a prophecy of “Enoch, the seventh from Adam” (Jude 1:14) from the Book of Enoch. The refrain “and then he died” echoes the warning of 2:17.

translation.meaning: Generations, descendants, family history: literally ‘begettings.’ Genesis is built on ten sections that begin ‘These are the generations of…’ (2:4; 5:1; 6:9 and on).
To walk. Here in a form that means to walk about, to live one’s whole life with someone. Noah too walked with God (6:9).
To comfort, console; also to be sorry, to relent. Lamech names Noah (noach, rest) with a play on this word.

A name could carry a hope or a prayer.

Aramaic copies of the Book of Enoch were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls.

overview.discussion: In a list where everyone dies, one line stands out: “Enoch walked with God” (v.24). What would it look like for my ordinary days to be described that way?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters. Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
